references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the parable of the sower, where Jesus tells about the sower who went out to sow, and some seed fell along the path and the birds came and ate it up.
Mark's parallel account of the parable of the sower, with the same image of the sower scattering seed and some of the grain falling along the path and being eaten by the birds.
Isaiah uses the image of seed and sowing as a metaphor for God's word going out and not returning empty, but accomplishing what God desires – a background for Jesus' parable of the sower.

Jesus' own explanation of the parable: The seed is God's word, and what fell along the path represents those who hear, but the devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts so that they may not believe and be saved.

Matthew's version of Jesus' explanation of the parable, where what was sown along the path is the one who hears the message about the kingdom without understanding it, and the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in the heart.
Mark's version of the explanation: The sower sows the word, and those by the path are those who hear the word, but Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

The preacher urges to sow one's seed in the morning and not let the hand rest in the evening – an image of faithful sowing without knowing what will succeed, relevant to the parable's theme of the sower's faithful work.
The psalmist speaks of sowing with tears and reaping with joy – an image of sowing and harvesting that forms the background for Jesus' parable of the sower and the various outcomes of the sowing.
